checks.description: The restored database (after migrations, before reapplication) has the same row counts, archive revision and surviving-run data as the database at backup time
Runs A and B exist in the restored backup with their points, summary and share, and have no tombstone: the backup really contains data deleted later
The first reapplication deleted the two resurrected runs, restored the marker of the run that never reached the backup, and reported no other outcome
After reapplication, deleted runs have no runs, run_points, run_summaries or run_shares rows
After reapplication, every deleted run has a tombstone
No tombstone expires earlier than one year after its deletion instant
The archive revision advanced exactly once per run that was actually deleted, and not for a restored marker
The surviving run is unchanged and the table counts moved only by the deleted runs
The second reapplication changed nothing: every entry reported marker_present and none was deleted again
The database state after the second reapplication is identical to the state after the first: same rows, tombstone expiry, archive revision and journal
The owner, runtime and maintenance roles exist and can log in
The three application roles are not superuser, have no BYPASSRLS, CREATEDB, CREATEROLE or REPLICATION
The runtime and maintenance roles have no access to the deletion journal table or the reapplication function
The runtime and maintenance roles cannot connect to the restored database: it stays closed until current permissions are restored (P12.4)
No application login has a session on the restored database
PostGIS is installed and callable in the restored database
Every migration file of this repository is recorded as applied
The original journal directory is byte-identical to what the exporter wrote
The read-only recovery copy of the journal was not modified by reapplication
The source database was not used after the simulated loss
